analysis.title: IT Hardware and Communications Equipment: Implied AI Multiples – Multiples Reset Again
key_insights: Since the October 12 update, Barclays' 12 AI-bucketed stocks have fallen 20% on average versus SPX down 2% and NDX down 6%. The average implied AI multiple fell to 24x from 35x.
7 of the 12 AI-bucketed names (FN, CLS, CIEN, JBL, FLEX, KEYS, GLW) are at trough implied AI multiples since tracking began in February.
FLEX, FN and CLS had the largest declines since the prior update, down 35%, 31% and 25%. DELL and CIEN are each down 21%.
The group is about 35% below peak stock prices on average, but still up about 52% YTD versus SPX up 11%.

For several names the implied AI multiple is approaching the multiple assigned to the core business, which implies much less AI valuation premium than earlier in the year. FLEX implies no premium for its AI-related business, which is being spun out.
The reset is broad but EMS names in particular carry less AI premium, while cloud/AI growth expectations remain strong. Optical multiples have also compressed materially from mid-year peaks.
The AI-bucketed companies represent about 19% of total Cloud/AI capex per Barclays estimates.
Average cloud AI revenue CAGR for 2023-27E is about 67% versus the initial estimate of about 53%, after higher hyperscaler capex expectations in the latest earnings round.

Non-AI names (AAPL, GRMN, AXON, MSI etc.) are up 1% on average since October 12, and up 5% excluding P and NTAP. P and NTAP are down 21% and 10% after previously running on AI on-prem and neocloud opportunity.
Barclays' industry view on IT Hardware and Communications Equipment is Neutral.
